topic: Aviation - runway numbers (magnetic heading divided by ten)
question: WHAT DOES THE NUMBER
ON THE RUNWAY MEAN?
options: Its length in hundreds of meters
The order it was built in
answer_full: Its compass direction, rounded and divided by ten
recap: Every runway has a giant number painted on each end, like twenty-seven on one side and zero-nine on the other.
explain: The number is the runway's compass heading, divided by ten and rounded. Twenty-seven means about two hundred seventy degrees, so the planes are heading west.
The other end of the same runway points the opposite way, exactly one hundred eighty degrees around. That's ninety degrees, so it says zero-nine: east.
The numbers follow the magnetic compass, and Earth's magnetic field slowly drifts. When it drifts far enough, the airport has to paint new numbers.
